issues.title: Agro yield % changes use the wrong base
issues.detail: Agro Tables 12 and 13 divide the change by the NEW year's yield. Table 13: estate 2.06 to 1.42 t/ha is printed -45% (text 5.6 repeats it) but is -31%; 10B 2.43 to 1.42 printed -71%, actually -42%; 11B -61% is -38%; 13C -58% is -37%. Table 12: 13C 19.57 to 23.31 printed +16%, actually +19%; mean 21.82 to 24.68 printed +12%, actually +13%.

issues.title: General charges RM/ha: 1,335.80 vs 1,330.80
issues.detail: PA Table 5 and text 5.1 give RM1,335.80/ha with Other Expenditure RM516.86/ha. Appendix 1 gives RM1,330.80/ha. RM2,336,484.34 / 1,755.70 ha = 1,330.80 and RM898,576.10 / 1,755.70 = 511.81, so Table 5 is wrong. Text 5.1 and item 4 also print the budget as 'RM1,1557.70' (should be RM1,557.70). Dashboard uses 1,330.80.

issues.title: Fertiliser programme: PA vs Agro disagree
issues.detail: Rock phosphate FY2025/26 programme: PA Table 11 297.00 mt; Agro Table 5 174.14 mt. Mix A applied: PA 495.43 mt vs Agro 494.43 mt (Agro program 495.4). Kieserite applied 101.70 (PA) vs 101.6 (Agro). Agro summary page says the FY2025/26 programme 'was completed fully' but its own Table 5 shows Mix B 97% and kieserite 98%. Mix B delivered: PA Table 11 says all 1,184.12 mt delivered (as at the 4 May 2026 visit), but Agro Table 5 (as of May 2026) shows only 1,165.53 mt delivered.

issues.title: Workers: 170 vs 177
issues.detail: PA Table 4, 4.1 and item 3 reply: 170 workers in April 2026. PA concluding remark 11.3 says 177 workers, which was the previous visit's figure.

issues.title: Yield typo 4.68 t/ha
issues.detail: PA comment item 14 reply: 'The yield of 4.68 per hectare'. Table 16 and 8.2: 24.68 t/ha.

issues.title: Agro field yields do not average to 24.68
issues.detail: Agro Table 12 field yields weighted by field hectares give 24.96 t/ha (about 43,830 t) against the printed mean 24.68 and PA FFB 43,322.41 t (24.68 t/ha). Table 13 (May 2026) does reconcile (1.42).

issues.title: Weather: PA heavy rain vs Agro dry spell
issues.detail: PA 6.1.1.2 and 6.1.2.2 blame incomplete spraying on heavy rain Nov 2025–Mar 2026. Agro 6.3 calls Jun 2025–Mar 2026 a prolonged dry period; its Table 14 shows Mar 2026 35 mm (3 days), Feb 172 mm, Jan 182 mm, but Dec 409 mm. Agro's own reply (item 6) also blames weeding delay on 'prolonged rainfall', contradicting its 6.3.

issues.title: PA manuring delivered total 2,227.3 vs 2,334.51
issues.detail: PA Table 11 main section: every line delivered equals required, but the delivered total is printed 2,227.3 (the applied total). The summary section prints delivered 2,334.51.

issues.title: Agro planted area 1,755.50 vs 1,755.70
issues.detail: Agro Table 1 'Total planted 1,755.50' while mature is 1,755.70 and Table 2 / PA give 1,755.70; 1,755.70 + 461.78 unplanted = 2,217.48 gross, so 1,755.50 is a typo.

issues.title: Block label errors
issues.detail: Agro Table 2 lists the last 2013C sub-block as C21 (47.37 ha); PA Table 2 and Agro Appendix give C42. PA 7.4 assigns the fourth gang to 'C34 to C22' (should be C42). PA photos 5–6 say fields 2028A1 and 2028A5 (2008A). Agro pruning/weeding checklists list 2010B blocks under '10A'. PA 6.1.1.3 lists circles due in '2008A11', but A11 is in 2010A (PA photo 1-2 caption: 2010A11).

issues.title: Palm counts and Ganoderma deaths inconsistent
issues.detail: Agro Table 3 census 209,811 palms vs 209,854 previous (43 fewer, all in 11A -9, 11B -32, 13C -2), yet Table 4 records 79 palms dead/removed this FY, mostly in other fields (A08 36, A02 9, B24 8) whose census is unchanged. Agro 2.4: 49 palms died of Ganoderma; Table 11 Ganoderma census: 48. Agro Table 9 pruning base 210,910 palms; Appendix 1 total palms sum to 212,575.

issues.title: Wrong period labels
issues.detail: PA 6.3.4: pest and disease cost 'as of September 2025' but the figure is Table 6's FY to April 2026. Agro Appendix 1 is titled FY2026/2027 but its month headers run May-25 to Apr-26. Agro 3.4 says FY26/27 progress 'as of June 2026', Table 6 heading says May 2026.

issues.title: Entertainment overspend RM4,792.91 vs RM4,795.91
issues.detail: PA 5.2(e) gives RM4,792.91 (192%); Appendix 1 Entertainment/Greeting/Foods variance RM4,795.91 (7,295.91 vs 2,500).

issues.title: Harvesting rounds range 23–40 vs table 18.10–43.00
issues.detail: PA 7.7 says 23 to 40 rounds in 12 months; Table 14 shows to-date rounds from 18.10 (C42) to 43.00 (A11), with A13 42.50. Similarly PA 6.1.2.2 says selective spraying reached '2.0 rounds' while Table 9 shows 2.10.

issues.title: Staff list vs text 3.2
issues.detail: PA 3.2 describes 1 Estate Manager, 2 Assistant Managers, 5 Field Conductors, 1 Chief Clerk, 1 General Clerk and 1 Mechanic, but Table 3 lists 1 Assistant Manager plus 1 Cadet Assistant, no Chief Clerk and 2 General Clerks.

actions.item: Complete FY2025/26 Mix B balance (73.60 mt) and start FY2026/27 Mix A/B once delivered
Use old stock: NK Mix 31.15 mt at 2 kg (hilly ex-rehab blocks), Mycoplex 280 kg on block 8, Borate 600 kg on block 41
Free machinery for fertiliser transport (only 1 trip/100 bags a day); move bags to harvest paths by mini tractor/Badang
Surface agricultural roads with crusher run (MLP5 quarry), prioritise busiest roads
Outsource internal FFB transport (still negotiating); consider rubber-track Badang 1.5–2.0 t for steep areas
Keep harvesting intervals at 12–15 days (PA) / within standard; watch 13C and 11B; cut unripe bunches and clear loose fruit at platforms
Resume Ganoderma deboling when machinery is free; monitor Carbon Fertilizer trial (1.5 L/palm)
Systematic thinning of runts and VOPs field by field (2 workers, 100 ml glyphosate/palm)
Pay pruning every 3 months instead of yearly
Rat census every 3 months; bait above 10%
Follow-up spraying for Clidemia, Asystasia, giant grass, VOPs; continue epiphyte control (A05, A08)
Identify vacant areas for supplying in FY2026/27

kb:
MLP 3 ESTATE (Millian Labau Plantation 3), United Malacca Berhad (UMB), Sabah. Fact pack from PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisor En Adnan Bin Mustafa; visit 4 May 2026; review period May 2025 to April 2026, Financial Year 2025/2026, 12 months; previous PA visit 27-28 October 2025) and Agronomy Report 1/2026 (Junior Agronomist En Alison Bin Janari, Senior Agronomist Mr Chong Kuan Ming; visit 29 May 2026; previous Agro visit 2/2025 on 23 October 2025; reviews manuring programme 2026/2027). Senior Manager Mr Celestine Sipilis (Agro spells it Celestine Bin Siplis). Estate run by Mr Tony Tiwon, Senior Assistant Manager In-charge (PA calls him Estate Manager). The UMB financial year runs May to April.

AREA (PA Table 1, Agro Table 1). Title area 2,217.48 ha. Planted 1,755.70 ha, all mature (79.18%). Roads 241.74 ha, unplantable 212.67 ha, buildings/others 7.37 ha. Agro splits unplanted 461.78 ha: roads 241.74, building and settlement 7.37, steep/hilly 141.82, swamps/pond 62.50, river/drainage 8.35. Plantings: 2007A 96.75 ha, 2008A 181.84, 2009A 164.26, 2010A 110.33, 2011A 281.40, 2009B 58.13, 2010B 240.95, 2011B 206.64, 2013C 415.40. Three divisions: A 834.58 ha, B 505.72 ha, C 415.40 ha. Palms aged 12 to 18 years (PA) / within 8-19 year category (Agro), mostly hilly, some extremely steep areas without terraces. No area change; rehabilitation completed; no replanting planned for next FY (PA). Agro: vacant areas in recently rehabilitated blocks, no supplying planned yet; identification of vacant areas continuing, supplying in FY2026/27. Agro Table 1 prints total planted 1,755.50 (typo).

PALM CENSUS (Agro Table 3): 209,811 palms, 120 SPH (previous 209,854). SPH by field: 07A 126, 08A 122, 09A 127, 09B 134, 10A 114, 10B 125, 11A 113, 11B 110, 13C 119. Thinning (Agro Table 4): 79 palms dead or removed this FY as of October 2025, 1,201 cumulative; 49 died of Ganoderma (BSR). Largest cumulative thinning A17 127 (2009A), A20 118 (2011A), C40 81, C34 80, C38 76, A16 68.

STAFF (PA Table 3): 11 staff incl. Tony Tiwon (G11), Assistant Manager Bairy Samun (G9), Cadet Assistant Raymond Jamian (G7), mechanic, 5 field conductors, 2 general clerks (Lily Florish Jell joined October 2025). Satisfactory.

LABOUR (PA Table 4, April 2026): 170 workers vs 184 required (-14), down from 177 at last visit; 1 worker per 10 ha. Harvesters 94 vs 98 (-4), down from 96; 1 harvester per 19 ha of mature; 4 more needed for steep terrain (1:18). Drivers 9 vs 12, heavy machinery operators 2 vs 4, manuring 15 (1 per 117 ha), sprayers 20 (1 per 88 ha), sprayers also used on manuring. PA concluding remark 11.3 wrongly says 177 workers.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Table 5, Appendix 1, FY2025/26 to April 2026). Actual RM2,336,484.34 vs budget RM2,734,858 (-15%). Staff salary and related RM761,504.41 (RM433.73/ha) vs 833,235 (474.59); labour and amenities RM676,403.83 (385.26/ha) vs 923,588 (526.05); other expenditure RM898,576.10 vs 978,035 (557.06/ha). Per ha: Appendix 1 RM1,330.80 vs budget RM1,557.70; Table 5 and text print RM1,335.80 (arithmetic gives 1,330.80). Over-budget lines: staff EPF +RM9,803.50 (12%, staff bonus EPF under-budgeted); labour EPF +RM5,908 (15%, foreign worker EPF); general office expenses +RM29,684.94 (52%, professional fees RM12.50 to RM14.00, air fares for Planting Advisor, EIA, quarry operations); subscription +RM1,273.23 (34%, MPOA, MEF, MEOA 2026); entertainment +RM4,795.91 (192%, reversed journals May-June 2025, reclassification, CEO/ED visits). Largest items: staff salary RM491,730.51, water/electricity RM330,768.24, labour paid leave RM302,672.40, cess/rate/rent RM116,964.11, labour welfare RM117,070.38, labour recruitment RM113,266.23 (budget 286,699), security RM99,970.88. RM per tonne: 53.93 vs 62.33 budget.

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Table 6): total RM4,376,373.05, RM2,492.67/ha vs budget RM4,840,776, RM2,757.18/ha. Per ha actual vs budget: supervision 22.68/35.32, weeding 188.50/229.24 (82%, behind schedule), manuring 1,408.89/1,504.85 (-6%), pest and disease 2.76/11.10, census and thinning 2.01/14.86, drains 7.45/56.73 (13%, excavator rental), bridges and culverts 42.85/73.42 (58%), roads 692.25/659.86 (+5%, RM1,215,397.78), boundaries 1.96/3.99, soil/water conservation 0.01/22.85, tools 5.85/10.10, supplying 6.37/14.06, pruning 111.08/120.79 (-8%). RM per tonne 101.02 vs 110.32.

WEEDING (PA 6.1, Agro 4.4). Circle and path spraying 4,776.35 of 5,267.10 ha programmed, 2.72 of 3 rounds, 91%. Lowest 2010A 72% (2.17 rds) and 2008A 77%. Glyphosate by knapsack (Inter Pump), 4.0 ha per man-day at RM20/ha = RM80/day. Circles due in 2008A15, 2008A11 (printed so; A11 is in 2010A), 2008A1, 2011A20. Selective (blanket interrow) 3,685.50 ha, 2.10 rounds, 70%: Kenlon (triclopyr) 150 ml + Emly (metsulfuron) 40 g per 10 L by mist blower, 5.0 ha per man-day, RM100/day. Only 2009B completed 3 rounds. Interrow improved, Nephrolepis and soft grasses establishing; keep 4-month interval. Jungle tree poisoning 954.14 ha (109% of 0.5 round programme) with triclopyr. PA blames heavy rain Nov 2025 to Mar 2026. Agro Table 10 by division: circle A 88%, B 94%, C 91%; interrow A 68%, B 74%, C 68%; Agro blames machinery shared with other operations. Agro: circles clean in B24, B25, A09, A05, A08, A20; debris in A05; Clidemia hirta, Asystasia, giant grass and VOPs in interrows; Clidemia in A05 not fully controlled; large epiphytes in A05, A08 and jungle boundary.

MANURING. PA Table 11 FY2025/26: programme 2,334.51 mt, applied 2,227.30 mt (95%). Mix A 495.43 applied fully; Mix B 1,110.52 of 1,184.12 (Feb 2026 round 297.95 of 371.55, balance 73.60); NK Mix 222.65 of 253.80 (FY24/25 C42, 31.15 left); kieserite 101.70 of 104.16; rock phosphate 297.00. Bucket application by 15 workers, 16-18 bags (3.5-4.0 ha) per man-day at RM17.50/ha. Agro Table 5 (to May 2026): Mix A 494.43 of 495.4 (100%), Mix B 1,144.83 of 1,184.12 applied, 1,165.53 delivered (97%), kieserite 101.6 of 104.16 (98%), RP 174.14 of 174.14 (100%). Last Mix B consignment received 28 April 2026; balance to finish by June 2026. FY2026/27 (Agro Table 6): Mix A 220.13 mt and Mix B 379.44 mt for May not started (late delivery); kieserite 90.47 mt applied (100%), 181.26 delivered. Quality check in B24/B25 (Mix B 1.0 kg/palm, April 2026 round) satisfactory; only 10 bags per worker per day because one machine trip (about 100 bags) a day, machinery shared with weeding and crop evacuation. Store well kept. Old stock to use (Agro Table 7): NK Mix (10.5:30) 31.15 mt at 2.00 kg on blocks 30, 31, 32, 21, 38, 37 (hilly ex-rehab); Mycoplex 280 kg at 0.11 kg on block 8 (Ganoderma); Borate 600 kg at 0.10 kg on block 41. Fertiliser recommendation FY2026/27 unchanged (Agro 7.1).

FERTILISER PROGRAMME FY2026/27 (Agro Appendix 1, kg/palm; months printed May-25 to Apr-26). 2007A: Mix A 2.20, KIE 1.00, Mix B 2.00, Mix A 2.20, Mix B 2.00. 2008A12/15 and 2009A/2009B/2010A: Mix A 2.20, KIE 1.00, RP 1.50 (not 2008A12/15), Mix B 2.20 (A8, A14 2.00), Mix A 2.20, Mix B 2.20. 2008A1 and A5: 9.00* Mix A in May plus RP 1.50. 2010B: Mix B 2.20 x3 with KIE 1.00 and RP 1.50; B30 9.00* plus RP. 2011A, 2011B, 2013C: Mix B 2.20 (May), KIE 1.00 (some blocks), Mix B 2.00 (Aug), RP 1.50 (Oct), Mix B 2.20 (Nov), Mix B 2.00 (Feb); B31 9.00* plus RP. Mix A 9.45:0:24:4; Mix B 9.45:0:24:3.7:0.48; kieserite 27% MgO; RP 28-30%. The asterisk is not explained.

PESTS AND DISEASES. PA: no serious rat or bagworm; slight Ganoderma; rat census every 3 months, bait above 10%. Cost RM4,854.46 (RM2.76/ha) for planting beneficial plants. Agro: pests under control; Ganoderma main concern, 48 dead palms in A02, A04, A05, A08, B23, B24 (Table 11); no deboling since the previous demonstration as machinery went to road repair; Carbon Fertilizer trial 1.5 L per palm on infected palms. A08 Ganoderma palms weak, small bunches, thin trunks.

PRUNING. PA Table 12: 1,621.53 of 1,755.70 ha (92.36%); lowest 2010A 83.72%, 2011B 84.29%, 2011A 86.79%. Progressive pruning by harvesters, paid once a year; PA recommends quarterly payment. Agro Table 9 (to April 2026): 191,182 of 210,910 palms (91%); 09B 62%, 11B 80%, 10B 87%, 09A 106%. Canopy acceptable, slight over-pruning in places; frond stacking improved but fertiliser should stay in the palm circle.

ROADS, DRAINS, BOUNDARIES (PA). Main road passable; agricultural roads lack crusher run, slippery and impassable when wet. Prioritise grading and surfacing busiest roads; crusher run from MLP5 quarry nearby and cheaper. Drains satisfactory, 48 excavator hours. Census and thinning RM3,526 (RM2.01/ha); assign 2 workers to thin runts and VOPs with 100 ml glyphosate per palm. Boundary marking Divisions B and C RM3,439; watch FFB thieves on the village-used main road.

HARVESTING (PA section 7, Agro 4.1). 4 gangs: A01-A09 19 harvesters with 3 mini crawlers; A10-A20 23; B21-B33 30; C34-C42 22, using wheelbarrows. PA Table 14: to-date rounds 18.10 (C42) to 43.00 (A11); intervals 10-16 days with some 8-9 days (to use dry days in steep areas). Keep 12-15 days; consider rubber-track Badang (1.5-2.0 t). Agro Table 8: early FY2025/26 long intervals (11B 20-27 days, 10B 16-28, 09B 16-24, 13C up to 17-28); improved from October 2025; May 2026 mostly 6-13 days, 13C 10-17, 11B 8-15. Crop quality B25 at 14-day interval: platforms 100%, 90% and 98% ripe (up to 10% unripe). Loose fruit collection satisfactory but some left at platforms. PA photos: FFB left on platform in 2013C35 because the lorry bin could not pass.

HARVESTING COST (PA Table 15, RM/t). Supervision 4.00 (budget 5.00), harvesting own FFB 55.33 (53.00), infield loading 5.06 (6.53), ramp maintenance 3.58 (3.10), internal transport 28.91 (21.35, RM1,252,656.53), tools 0.82 (1.03); subtotal 97.71 vs 90.01 (+9%). External transport 36.57 vs 42.60 (outsourced). Total RM5,817,459 = RM134 vs RM133 (Table 17: 134.28 vs 132.61). Internal transport overrun due to steep terrain and rain-damaged roads; internal transport outsourcing still under negotiation.

CROP PRODUCTION (PA Table 16, FY2025/26 May 2025 to April 2026). FFB 43,322.41 t vs budget 43,878.00 (-1%); last year 38,309.69 t. CPO 8,802.53 t (budget 8,942.34; last year 7,836.51); kernel 1,925.33 t. OER 20.32% (budget 20.38, LY 20.46); KER 4.44%. Yield 24.68 t FFB/ha vs 24.99 budget and 21.82 last year; CPO 5.01 t/ha (budget 5.09, LY 4.46).

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA Table 17, RM per tonne FFB, ex-estate). FY2025/26: general charges 53.93 (budget 62.33), upkeep 101.02 (110.32), harvesting and collection 134.28 (132.61), total 289.23 vs 305.26 (-5%). FY2024/25: 57.98, 112.74, 134.54, total 305.26 (budget 317.69). Satisfactory due to high crop.

VEHICLES (PA Table 18). Management vehicles acceptable.
